title: Pre-Analysis — Vacuum Toilet Assembly Standard and the Aft Lavatory Drain Interface
abstract: Closed pre-analysis examining whether the current vacuum toilet assembly standard can absorb the aft lavatory drain interface complaint that was raised as an internal order and closed without a modification.

sections.objective: Establish whether the recurrent corrosion reported at the aft lavatory drain interface can be addressed within the existing vacuum toilet assembly standard, by extending its effectivity and adding the drain interface to its scope, rather than by raising a separate structural change. The internal order that reported the corrosion was closed without a modification a year ago, and the operator has since asked twice more, so the question was reopened from the product side rather than from the structures side.
sections.findings_summary: Three items were confirmed and the answer to the question was yes, with a caveat that belongs to another office. The toilet assembly standard reaches the drain line as far as the shroud but stops at the fuselage penetration, which is where the corrosion actually is; extending the assembly scope covers the clamp and the shroud but not the shell. The servicing task and the retrofit bulletin both follow that boundary and change together. The third item is the published external doubler repair on the aft lower shell, which several of the affected aircraft already carry: a repaired shell moves the drain clamp positions by up to twenty millimetres and the extended assembly has to accommodate that or it will not fit on the very aircraft that need it most.
sections.next_steps: The extension was cleared to proceed for the clamp and shroud, with the shell penetration left to the structures office and the internal order reopened against that scope rather than closed a second time. The assembly design was asked to accept the repaired shell clamp positions as a design case rather than as a concession, since a quarter of the affected aircraft already carry the repair. The bulletin and the servicing task will be revised together once the clamp envelope is fixed.

similarity_seeds: corrosion at a lavatory drain penetration
waste line clamp and shroud at the fuselage shell

tasks.title: Establish where the assembly scope ends and the structure begins
Search waste and lower shell data around the drain penetration
Count the affected aircraft that already carry a shell repair

expected_findings.rationale: Retrieved on the aft lower shell zone alone; the two documents have no vocabulary in common. The external doubler repair raises the local skin thickness and moves the drain clamp positions by up to twenty millimetres, and a quarter of the affected aircraft already carry it.
expected_findings.resolution: Accept the repaired shell clamp positions as a design case for the extended assembly rather than handling each aircraft by concession.

expected_findings.rationale: The servicing and functional check follows the same scope boundary as the assembly and stops at the shroud. If the clamp and shroud come into the assembly scope the task has to gain the clamp torque and the shroud seal check, neither of which is described anywhere today.
expected_findings.resolution: Revise the task with the bulletin once the clamp envelope is fixed, adding the clamp torque and the shroud seal check.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin is written aircraft by aircraft against the twelve aircraft that took the supplier change. Extending the assembly scope changes what the bulletin installs without changing which aircraft it applies to, which its present structure cannot express in a revision bar.
expected_findings.resolution: Reissue the bulletin at a new revision with the clamp and shroud work as a separate accomplishment block.

expected_non_findings.reason: Shares the vestibule zone and is retrieved on every zone search of that area because the equipment rack and the lavatory sit either side of the same monument. The head end architecture has no waste line, no drain and no interface with the lavatory module.

type_data.conclusion: Issued 2026-07-13. The clamp and shroud can be absorbed into the assembly standard; the shell penetration goes back to the structures office with the internal order reopened against it.
